clue.text: Awful smell coming from small freshwater fish

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
the tench is a European freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: A dreadful pong rising from a little river fish someone has left out.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong and very unpleasant odour, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Head of state rests uneasily showing strain

indicators.note: something resting uneasily shifts about, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged
'Head of' keeps only the first letter of 'state'

blocks.note: the first letter of state
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A national leader sleeps badly, visibly worn down by the pressures of office.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress and strain are both words for mental or physical pressure and tension.

clue.text: Develop complex

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to work out in more detail
second meaning: an adjective, intricate and detailed

explanation.surface: An instruction to build a compound, perhaps a housing estate or a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the adjective are spelt alike but pronounced differently: the verb ends in a long 'ate', the adjective in a short one.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate is to expand on something in detail, and an elaborate plan is an intricate, involved one.

clue.text: Mysterious tomb, one discovered by leader of Crusades

indicators.note: 'leader of' keeps only the first letter of 'Crusades'

blocks.note: a crypt is an underground burial chamber
the Roman numeral for one
the first letter of Crusades

explanation.surface: A puzzling grave unearthed by a medieval crusading commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered by' just places the leader's letter after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic means having a hidden or obscure meaning, hence puzzling or enigmatic.

clue.text: Charm, a cross, last in market

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is wanted, not the whole word

blocks.note: taken as written
a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey
the final letter of market

explanation.surface: A list of trinkets on sale at a stall: a lucky charm, a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' suggests a crucifix, fitting the charm; here it means a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a small object worn as a charm to ward off evil or bring luck.

clue.text: Bullfighter in form at a do recently

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning their boundaries

blocks.note: concealed across form, at, a, do and recently

explanation.surface: A bullfighter who was on top form at a recent party.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the performer who kills the bull in a Spanish bullfight.

clue.text: Knight having no chance to find weapon

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken away from the word before

blocks.note: Sir Lancelot, knight of King Arthur's Round Table
a lot is a chance or fate, as in casting lots

explanation.surface: A knight with no hope of victory goes looking for something to fight with.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing LOT from the end of Arthur's knight Lancelot leaves the answer, appropriately his own weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is the long spear carried by a mounted knight when jousting or charging.

clue.text: Paper in stand is English

blocks.note: to stand someone a drink is to treat them
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A newspaper on a newsstand is an English one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' looks like a newspaper; it means a scholarly written study.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written essay or study of a subject, an academic paper.

clue.text: Prepared to study unknown quantity

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
x, y and z are unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: A student all set to tackle an algebra problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready and prepared both mean set up and fit for action.

clue.text: Material wealth

blocks.note: first meaning: physical matter, stuff
second meaning: riches

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it looks like 'material wealth', worldly riches; it splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Substance is matter of a particular kind, and also possessions or means, as in a man of substance.

clue.text: Make fit for use low sort of accommodation

blocks.note: to service a machine is to maintain it in working order
flat means low and level

explanation.surface: Instructions to renovate a cheap, basic kind of lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: A service flat is a British term for a rented apartment that comes with cleaning and other housekeeping provided.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a type of apartment where domestic services are included in the rent.

clue.text: Preferred feathers delivered from London?

blocks.note: to prefer charges is to bring them against someone
down is a bird's soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Choosing quilts filled with plumage that were shipped out from the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage one travels 'down' from London to the provinces, so goods sent out of the capital are fancifully carried down; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought means delivered, and British convention treats London as up, so anything leaving it goes down.

clue.text: Scout, first to salute English dramatist

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of salute
Dennis Potter, English writer of The Singing Detective

explanation.surface: A Boy Scout is the first to salute a famous English playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scout' suggests the youth movement; here it means a lookout or talent finder.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotter, like a scout, is someone who watches out for and identifies things or talent.

clue.text: Daughter coming in to mend broken piece

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one part is placed inside another
something broken is in pieces, so the preceding letters are put back together differently

blocks.note: the six letters rearranged
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl comes round to repair something that has broken.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of 'to mend' is split after OD to let the daughter's D in.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover bit or scrap, a piece remaining from something larger.

clue.text: Notice what's given to departing soldiers?

blocks.note: first meaning: a dismissal, being told to leave a job
second meaning, taken literally: the instructions troops receive to set off

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second meaning as a literal reading of an idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given one's marching orders is an idiom for being sacked, which is getting one's notice.

clue.text: Forceful eastern regent implicated in charge

indicators.note: being implicated means being mixed up in something, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
the six letters rearranged
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A powerful Oriental ruler is accused of involvement in a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests an accusation, chiming with 'implicated'; it is the abbreviation IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Energetic means full of vigour and force, so forceful is a near synonym.

clue.text: Be quick, or set point's lost

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: all eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A tennis coach urges a player to hurry or the set point will slip away.
explanation.definitionFit: Step on it is an idiom from pressing the accelerator, meaning hurry up.

clue.text: Come onto the stage in theatre in revised Osborne play

indicators.note: in places one part inside the letters of the following words
a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters rearranged
an actor's entrance is marked Enter in a script

explanation.surface: An actor's cue to walk on in a theatre staging a revival of an Osborne drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of 'theatre in' splits after THE to take the stage direction inside.
explanation.definitionFit: John Osborne wrote this 1957 play about the faded music-hall performer Archie Rice.

clue.text: Gathers in information over savings

indicators.note: in places the first part inside the word for information
in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the result reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
to gather is to get or collect

explanation.surface: Someone collects financial information about their savings.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is a sum of money saved up for the future.

clue.text: A whole number teeing off close to marker

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters before it are out of order
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

blocks.note: the six letters rearranged
the final letter of marker

explanation.surface: A golfer teeing off near a numbered course marker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teeing off' looks like a single golf phrase, but 'off' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a number with no fractional part, a whole number.

clue.text: Smart spook snatching short sleep

indicators.note: snatching means grabbing and holding, so one word takes another inside it

blocks.note: a spook is slang for a spy
a nap is a brief sleep

explanation.surface: A well-dressed secret agent grabs forty winks on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' could mean clever or well dressed; it is the stylish sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy can mean stylish or smart, as in a snappy dresser.

clue.text: Soldier, in consequence, left umbrella

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper
so means therefore, as a result
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A soldier, as a result, abandoned his brolly.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella carried to give shade from the sun.

clue.text: Ladies' man finding note in changing room

indicators.note: in places the note inside the other letters
changing means altering the letters into a different order

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A womaniser leaves a love letter in the changing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing room' reads as one place, but 'changing' is the anagram signal for 'room'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romeo, after Shakespeare's hero, is a man known for romancing women.

clue.text: Figure old scam must take in mark

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the word for scam surrounds the next part

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a con is a swindle
a tag is a label or identifying mark

explanation.surface: A figure on an old fraud must take in a mark, the swindler's target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' hints at a con artist's victim, fitting the scam; it is a label.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is a geometric figure with eight sides.

clue.text: Frozen, enter resort to make a political address

indicators.note: re-sort means sort again, putting the letters into a fresh order

blocks.note: numb with cold
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Chilled visitors arrive at a holiday spot to deliver a campaign speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place; read as re-sort it means rearrange. 'Address' is a location, not a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Number Ten Downing Street is the official residence of the British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Rouse oneself and dress

blocks.note: first meaning: rise from bed
second meaning: an outfit, especially an odd one

explanation.surface: Morning routine: wake, then put clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' looks like a verb following on; it is the noun for a costume, written with a hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: To get up is to rise from bed, and a get-up is a set of clothes or costume.

clue.text: Hard to acquire right container for animals to drink out of

definitions.text: container for animals to drink out of

indicators.note: acquiring something means taking it in, so a letter is placed inside the word for hard

blocks.note: tough means difficult or hard
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: It's difficult to get hold of the correct water vessel for livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a long open box holding water or feed for farm animals.

clue.text: Little boy, after short time, becomes difficult

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a pet form of the name Richard

explanation.surface: A small child, after a brief period, starts to play up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the boy's name after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricky means awkward to deal with, needing skill or care.
